title: Rhyme and Emphatic Stress in English

blocks.text: Understanding rhyme and emphatic stress is essential for effective communication in English. These elements enhance clarity and expression in spoken language.

blocks.markdown: Rhyme refers to the similarity of sounds in the final syllables of words, often used in poetry and songs. For example, 'cat' and 'hat' rhyme because they share the same ending sound.

blocks.title: Definition of Rhyme
blocks.text: Rhyme is the repetition of similar sounds in the final syllables of words, typically used to create rhythm and musicality in language.

blocks.markdown: Emphatic stress involves placing emphasis on certain syllables in words or phrases to convey meaning or contrast. For instance, in the sentence 'I didn't say she stole my money,' stressing different words changes the implied meaning.

blocks.title: Identifying Rhymes
blocks.prompt: Choose the word that rhymes with 'light'.

steps.text: Consider the ending sound of 'light', which is '-ight'.
Look for options that have the same ending sound.

blocks.answer: The correct answer is 'fight', as it shares the '-ight' ending with 'light'.

blocks.markdown: To identify emphatic stress, pay attention to which syllable is pronounced louder or longer. This can change the meaning of a sentence significantly.

blocks.title: Tip for Emphatic Stress
blocks.text: When practicing emphatic stress, try saying sentences aloud, emphasizing different words to hear how the meaning shifts.

points: Rhyme enhances the musical quality of language and helps with memorization.
Emphatic stress is crucial for conveying the intended meaning and contrast in speech.
